messages:
alex.k: FYI Veridian POC reporting very slow TTFT on our hosted endpoint, seeing lots of 429s and some odd cache-miss logs.
anika.s: Ugh. Which model / route? Any reproducible curl we can run?
ale x.k: route: /v1/generate model: redwood-alpha-2 length: 512 batch_size: 1. Sample request: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-alpha-2\",\"input\":\"Hello\"}'` — happens intermittently, but TTFT jumps to 1.2s then 3s then 700ms.
anika.s: Can you paste the request-id from the logs? We need to trace through routing.
ale x.k: saw request-id: req_8d2f9a6c in the app logs at 2156789033, backtrace shows: `x-redwood-rt: slow-path` and `kv-cache: miss prefill`. Also a few `429 quota_exceeded` from the API.
nate_r: Do they have Dedicated or are they on hosted free tier? 429s could be hitting rate limits or token buckets if they burst.
ale x.k: Hosted, on pay-as-you-go. They expected small spikes but not sustained. Pricing/Q: client asked if reserved capacity would avoid this?
anika.s: Yes, Dedicated avoids shared rate limiting and gives predictable throughput. But let's troubleshoot first — maybe prefill/batching tuning will fix.
leo-m: Quick checklist: 1) confirm warmup/prefill disabled? 2) check client concurrency and retry logic, 3) look at batching window (we had recent default change), 4) verify KV cache TTL & namespace mapping.
ale x.k: Warmup is off. Client sends many single-token prompts concurrently (~50 concurrent). They do not use retries. Batching window is default 10ms I think. KV cache TTL 15m.
leo-m: 50 single-token concalls -> could cause queuing jitter and misaligned batching causing small micro-batches and more context switching. That increases tail latency and might trigger rate-limiter if worker pools saturate.
anika.s: Can we temporarily flip their route to a higher concurrency pool and enable prefill/persistent KV for the session? I can do a canary if ops approves.
nate_r: Ops: @deploy-bot can we route client veridian-account to the burst pool 3 for 30 minutes? Need to track impact on cost.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Routing change requested by anika.s — approved by policy. Applied: veridian-account -> pool-burst-3 (2156789050).
ale x.k: Thanks. After routing change I'm still seeing some 429s but TTFT reduced from 1.2s->0.45s median, tail 95% from 3s->0.9s. Cache-miss logs still present: `kv-cache: namespace=veridian_session missing key=precache/11`.
leo-m: That suggests prefill not populating before first token. Are they using a session token that changes per request? If so, cache key churn prevents hits.
anika.s: Ask client to pin session_id per conversation or enable shared conversation namespace. Also we can enable prefix caching for their route so common prompts get cached across sessions.
ale x.k: Client says they rotate session_id per user for privacy reasons. They can't pin a long-lived id. Security questionnaire flagged that they need ephemeral IDs.
nate_r: We can implement a short-lived shared key per account that expires in 1 minute — still respecting their privacy but improving cache hit rate. Prod change though — needs security sign-off.
anika.s: For immediate relief propose: 1) increase batching window to 25ms for route (reduces micro-batches), 2) enable ephemeral shared-prefix caching (account-scoped) with 60s TTL, 3) offer demo of Dedicated to show steady latency + pricing.
leo-m: I'll push batching window change (2156789065). Expect modest cost bump but big latency improvement for bursty single-token traffic.
ale x.k: Client questions on pricing: how much will a 30-day Dedicated trial cost vs hosted spikes? They want numbers to share with procurement.
anika.s: I'll send a calc: Dedicated baseline monthly commit = $Xk for 8k tokens/sec, for POC can do 14-day trial at 20% discount + usage overage at hosted rates. (I'll follow up in email).
nate_r: Also capture security note: ephemeral account-scoped cache key must be included in their security questionnaire answer — I'll draft wording: "we use ephemeral account-scoped identifiers to enable performance caching while isolating user data; keys expire after 60s and are auditable".
anika.s: Great. Back to ops: after batching bump we saw tails drop to 0.6s 95th and 0.25s median; 429 rate down by 78%.
ale x.k: Client is happy so far. They want a follow-up presales call tomorrow to review options and sign-off on the ephemeral cache approach. Can we have SRE on the call?
leo-m: I'll join. Nate can prepare the security blurb.
nate_r: I'll prepare the blurb and cost delta chart.
anika.s: Filing this as POC support case for handoff to AM after trial ends. Notes: request ids tracked: req_8d2f9a6c, req_8d2f9ad1, req_8d2f9b10.
ale x.k: Thanks team :thumbsup:
